positive_measure_identity: for H(t)=integral exp(-t lambda)dnu(lambda), D_(k,h)H(t)=integral exp(-t lambda)(1-exp(-h lambda))^k dnu(lambda)>=0
equivalence: for sufficiently smooth H, nonnegativity of all D_(k,h) for k>=0,h>0,t>0 is equivalent to complete monotonicity by division by h^k and h->0
arithmetic_advantage: finite differences use bounded spectral factors between zero and one and avoid differentiating infinite prime sums, which otherwise introduces powers of log(n)
hostile: H(t)=1-(1/2)exp(-pi^2 t) stays positive but fails the first difference inequality
residual_axes: finite-difference order k and step h are observer coordinates; arithmetic cutoff N remains independent
acceptance_test: Prove D_(k,h)H_explicit(t)>=0 for all rational positive t,h and every natural k, with completed endpoint-gamma-prime coupling and tail bounds that do not assume the representing positive measure.
